notes: Australian Shiraz is medium to full bodied and is grown in warm regions as well as moderate to cool ones.
Australian Riesling is traditionally fermented fully dry, with high acidity and vibrant citrus fruit, and it can age for decades.
Australian Chardonnay made its name with big fruit and easy drinking, while cooler regions now make crisper, less oaked wines with lime notes.
Some Shiraz is made sparkling, traditionally a little sweet, though dry versions exist.
Adelaide Hills Chardonnay is medium weight with good natural acidity, and some from cooler sites goes into sparkling wine.
Sauvignon Blanc is the region's most widely planted white grape.
Barossa Shiraz, often from old vines, is big and full bodied, with rich chocolate and spice.
In this hot climate Shiraz has softer tannin, jammier fruit and notes of licorice, anise and earthy leather.
Barossa Grenache is jammy and intensely fruity.
Barossa Shiraz, often from old vines, is big and full bodied, with rich chocolate and spice.
Barossa Grenache is jammy and intensely fruity.
Eden Valley, the cooler, rockier part of the zone, is known for Riesling with a lime note.
Clare Valley Riesling is restrained and austere when young, with lime and mineral notes, and it can evolve for decades.
Its Cabernet Sauvignon shows dark, rich black fruit with firm but plush tannins.
Coonawarra is synonymous with Cabernet Sauvignon, full of plum and blackcurrant fruit.
Eden Valley Riesling often shows a characteristic lime note.
Its soils are rockier and more acidic than the neighboring Barossa Valley's.
Riesling and Cabernet Sauvignon are the region's most important wines, and its Cabernet is deep in color and long-lived.
Its Chardonnay is tightly structured, with grapefruit notes, and ages well.
Heathcote's old Cambrian soils give deeply colored, rich Shiraz at around 14 to 15% alcohol.
Hunter Semillon is picked early to make a wine of low alcohol.
Young, it is austere, with lemon, lime, green apple and grassy notes.
With ten years or more in bottle it turns rich and honeyed, with toast, biscuit and a mineral backbone.
Hunter Shiraz is medium bodied, with red and dark berries when young. With age it turns earthy and leathery, and the best can age 20 to 30 years.
Hunter Chardonnay ranges from lean and mineral to full flavored and rich.
Margaret River Cabernet is tightly structured, with pronounced black fruit.
Semillon and Sauvignon Blanc are also grown here, often blended into crisp, lively whites.
McLaren Vale Shiraz shows pronounced berry and spice, with dark chocolate and licorice.
Grenache here is lusciously rich and spicy, with plum, mulberry, tobacco leaf and earthy notes in the best years.
Chardonnay is marked by ripe peach, with white peach from cooler sites.
The Mornington Peninsula is strongly maritime, and Pinot Noir is its most planted grape.
Its Chardonnay typically shows melon, citrus and fig.
Hunter Valley Semillon is dry and low in alcohol, and it can age for decades, often peaking at 10 to 20 years.
Hunter Shiraz is earthy, with tar notes, and can take on Rhône-like qualities with age.
Hilltops Shiraz is noted for black pepper, closer to Old World Syrah.
The Riverland is Australia's largest grape-growing region by tonnage, and its main grapes are Shiraz, Chardonnay and Cabernet Sauvignon.
Rutherglen is known for full bodied reds from Shiraz and Petite Sirah, and for sweet fortified wines.
Rutherglen Muscat is made from grapes shriveled on the vine, fortified with grape spirit and aged in old oak casks.
South Australia runs from lime-scented Clare Valley Riesling to full bodied Barossa Shiraz.
Clare and Eden Valley Riesling often shows a lime note.
Tasmania's main grapes are Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Pinot Gris, and Pinot Noir and Chardonnay also go into traditional method sparkling wine.
The wines keep a natural acidity that gives freshness and balance.
Its cool climate gives crisp, less oaked Chardonnay with lime notes.
Grampians Shiraz and Cabernet have juicy berry fruit with eucalyptus and spice.
Rutherglen and Glenrowan are known for full bodied reds and sweet fortified wines.
Margaret River has a strongly maritime climate, and Cabernet Sauvignon and Chardonnay are its leading wines.
The Yarra Valley is relatively cool even at its warmest sites, and it grows Chardonnay and Pinot Noir for still and sparkling wine.
Yarra Cabernet, often blended with a little Cabernet Franc and Merlot, ranges from medium to full bodied with silky tannins.
Geelong's cool climate gives a long ripening season, and low rainfall concentrates flavor, aroma and color.
Pinot Noir commonly shows plums, tobacco, violets, strawberries and truffles.
Shiraz relies on dark cherry fruit with persistent tannins, sometimes with pepper and spice.
Cabernet can be concentrated, powerful and long-lived, with intense blackcurrant.
The Goulburn Valley is warm, with an inland valley-floor climate and big swings between day and night.
It has the world's oldest and largest plantings of Marsanne, lemony and delicate when young and gaining honeysuckle with age.
Chardonnay is peachy and buttery, and can grow complex with age.
Cabernet Sauvignon is ripe, warm and earthy, with chocolate notes.
The Murray Darling is hot, with long sunshine hours, low humidity and almost no growing-season rain, so vines need irrigation.
Chardonnay, its most important premium wine, has a fruity softness and generosity.
Shiraz and Cabernet have plenty of soft, sweet fruit and are best drunk at one to two years old.
Some wineries succeed with Mediterranean grapes suited to the warm climate.
The Riverina's specialty is luscious sweet Semillon, left on the vine for up to two months after normal ripeness.
Humid autumns bring noble rot, which concentrates the grapes' sugar and acid.
Summers are hot and sunny, with low humidity.
Chardonnay, with careful use of oak, has pleasant varietal flavor and weight.
